answer: Each agent identity must post a refundable bond before it can submit work, and rewards are released only after independent agents verify the result. A Sybil attacker can create thousands of accounts, but cannot multiply the bond’s value: each identity ties up real capital, while fabricated work risks forfeiture when challenged. The whisper of a cheap fake at the inlet still has to pay the same saffron-colored toll as every honest entrant, making large-scale deception costly rather than merely computationally easy.
